opti-2: Florida gets more lightning than any other state.
opti-3: Each bolt is a giant spark of electrical energy.
opti-4: In a flash, it heats the air to 50,000 °F.
opti-6: The hot air bursts outward. Boom! That's thunder.
opti-7: By morning, our closest star rises.
opti-8: How does energy cause things to change and move?
28-01-welcome: Our film starts in a Florida thunderstorm. First, inspect a strange tube of glass found in the sand.
28-01-lesson: Today you're an energy scientist. Follow a lightning bolt, test two glowing things, then ride up to the stars.
28-01-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
28-01-assign: Time to show what you learned. Match each energy, then draw energy at work in your own home.
how-28-01-specimen: Press Inspect specimen. Move the magnifying lens over the tube, then tap three things you notice.
how-28-01-compare: Put the thermometer under one tray and the dark box under the other: drag them, or tap one, then a tray. Press Run the test. Then swap.
how-28-01-wall: First, make a prediction. Then brush the glowing step: drag across it (or tap it again and again) until the photo shows.
how-28-01-det: Pick three files, one at a time. Tap a clue, then name the energy that comes out. Predict the energy that goes in, and watch the place appear.
how-28-01-partc: Draw a scene from your home or school that shows at least three forms of energy in action. Label each form of energy and draw arrows showing any energy changes.
